text.p: Paint manufacturer Wattyl Ltd said on Thursday it expected improved results in the six months to June 30 in Australia, its main market.
Wattyl said it expected an improved profit performance in New Zealand and Asia was expected to show improved results.

The company also it expected to pay a higher tax rate in the U.S. following absorption of the remaining accumulated tax losses. Earlier, Wattyl reported a 16 percent rise in net profit to A$12.30 million in the six months ended December 31.

"Continued emphasis on improved customer service, release of new and improved products and efficiency gains in all segments of the operations are expected to provide the impetus for further improved results in the second half of this financial year," Wattyl said in relation to its Australian operations.
On the United States: "All divisions contributed to the profit increase and further improvement is expected in the second half of the year," it said.
On New Zealand: "Cost containment disciplines now in force should result in an improved profit performance during the remainder of the 1996/97 year," the paint maker said.

Wattyl said its performance in Asia was impeded by a substantial fall in sales and profits in Singapore resulting in sales across the region four percent below last year and profit before tax eight percent below 1995.
"The Asian region is expected to show improved results as the year progresses," Wattyl said.
At 3.25 p.m. (0425 GMT), Wattyl shares were seven cents higher at A$5.28.
